This is a very substantial review. This is about fairness in our tax system. It’s about trying to better align the taxes that people pay when they earn income through trusts versus when they earn income from working, from providing their labour. These are changes that have been called for by experts for decades. If we go back to major reviews in the 1970s and all the way through the Howard government, the Henry review, even the Abbott government’s review, these changes to trust taxation have been called for.I think he’s getting that from lots of corners. People are saying that the Liberal party needs to do better.The polls are showing that the Liberal party is at an all-time low. And so, things have to change. new_points.title: Fans hope to save ‘tartan fortress’ where Scotland football team first played
new_points.content: Part of site of First Hampden in Glasgow is up for rent and campaigners want to turn it into a community hubFans of Scotland’s national football team may not have had many reasons to celebrate in recent years, but that hasn’t always been the case. Almost 150 years ago, in 1878, the team moved into their first home in a Glasgow ground known as First Hampden and promptly won every game they played there.As well as being celebrated as Scotland’s “tartan fortress”, First Hampden, about half a mile from where Hampden Park sits today in south Glasgow, is widely considered the world’s first purpose-built international football stadium. Many features now commonplace in grounds around the world – including season tickets, turnstiles and pavilions – have long been thought to have originated there.

new_points.title: Why Abdul El-Sayed might not be winning Black voters in Michigan
new_points.content: The Michigan candidate for US Senate seat is running without directly acknowledging specific constituent groupsAbdul El-Sayed has an impressive résumé: Rhodes scholar, professor of epidemiology at Columbia University, executive director of the Detroit health department. And, at 41, the Michigan Democratic senatorial candidate represents a new generation of politicians, a shift that he also embodies sartorially. Whereas casual dress for many politicians is a tieless dress shirt with rolled up sleeves, El-Sayed has embraced a post-corporate, digital nomad-ish uniform: fitted black T-shirt, slim jeans and sneakers.His progressive politics are having a moment among liberals, and he remains unswervingly disciplined about his message: “Money Out of Politics, Money in Your Pocket, Medicare for All.” On paper he appears well-aligned to Democratic sensibilities in this moment, and he is competitive in the polls. But his support is softer than overall Democratic sentiment would dictate, especially among Black voters.

new_points.title: The Guardian view on the US, Russia and the international criminal court: Trump’s assault on the rule of law intensifies | Editorial
new_points.content: A fuel deal with Vladimir Putin, and sanctions against the legal institution, ram home the president’s belief that might is rightOn Friday, Donald Trump drove home his belief that might is right and the rule of law is an obstacle rather than an essential foundation stone of international order. First came the escalated assault on the international criminal court (ICC), sanctioning the body itself. Then he announced a deal with Russia to buy diesel.The US has long chafed at the notion of being bound by the rule of law that it espoused publicly. That hypocrisy now appears as a lesser vice. The president has declared that “my own morality” is all that constrains him. His brazen flouting of the law, embrace of dictators and rhetorical attacks all undermine global standards.Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? new_points.title: Bookmarked: Stories That Caught Our Eye This Week

new_points.title: Former US Envoy Warns of Wider Middle East Conflict
new_points.content: Former White House Middle East Coordinator Brett McGurk tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the deadly attack on Riyadh's international airport underscores the growing threat from Iran-backed Houthi militants, while hardline leadership in Tehran complicates efforts to negotiate an end to the broader regional conflict. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, McGurk discusses his new book, Brink, which recounts negotiations to free the October 7 hostages, and warns that the Trump administration's Russian diesel agreement could undermine efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

new_points.title: Saudi Airport Hit Again as Riyadh Set to Host Major Conferences

new_points.title: Globalization Defies a Decade of Populist Pushback
new_points.content: Bloomberg News Senior Economics Writer Shawn Donnan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that globalization has continued to expand despite a decade of populist policies, tariffs and efforts to reshape international trade following Brexit and President Donald Trump's first election victory. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Donnan says growing cross-border investment, global supply chains and digital technology demonstrate that the world economy remains increasingly interconnected despite political resistance.

new_points.title: Riyadh Airport Attack, Trump To Ukraine: “Time To Get A New President”
new_points.content: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Joined by Jason Horowitz - NYT Former Rome Bureau Chief, William Taylor - Atlantic Council Eurasia Center Distinguished Fellow, Jennifer Lee - BMO Capital Markets Senior Economist, Brett McGurk - Fmr NSC Coordinator for the Middle East, Ravi Gupta - Author, “The Invisible List”, and Leslie Shedd - Rising Communications President.

new_points.title: Tech Billionaires Gain $845 Billion in 2026
new_points.content: Bloomberg News Wealth Reporter Dylan Sloan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the world's technology billionaires gained a record $845 billion through the first nine months of 2026, while fortunes outside the sector declined by a combined $62 billion. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Sloan discusses how the AI boom is creating new billionaires in the US and China and explains how Bloomberg's relaunched Billionaires Index tracks the world's 500 richest people.

new_points.title: Saudi Airport Attack Raises Middle East War Risks

They also examine Ukraine's opposition to President Donald Trump's Russian diesel agreement, which Kyiv says could help finance Moscow's war, and the challenges facing negotiations to end the conflict.

new_points.title: Big Banks Face Test as Earnings Season Begins
new_points.content: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior US Banks Analyst Herman Chan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that major banks enter third-quarter earnings season with strong credit quality but face questions about the impact of higher interest rates, slowing investment banking activity and potential risks tied to AI financing. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Chan says wealth management could be a bright spot for banks including Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, while investors will also be watching for signs of credit deterioration and updates on executive succession plans.

new_points.title: Trump's Russia Diesel Deal Deepens Ukraine Rift

Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Taylor says European allies are increasing their support for Kyiv and argues that Ukraine needs greater access to military technology, including Starlink connectivity, to target Russian missile launchers.

new_points.title: Exclusive: Dimon, Farley, Gov. Whitmer on Rebuilding American Manufacturing

Michigan’s governor Gretchen Whitmer is hopeful that the partnership will provide more opportunities for the state’s workforce.
